stations.name: Star topology

tasks.q: What is at the centre of a star network?
a: A switch
A printer
A laptop
The internet
tasks.fb: Every device in a star connects to the central switch, and all data passes through it.

tasks.q: How does each device connect in a star network?
a: With its own cable to the central switch
With a cable to the next device along
With cables to every other device
Only by Bluetooth
tasks.fb: Each device has its own dedicated cable to the switch. Cables to every other device would be a full mesh.

bullets: Every device connects to a central switch with its own cable.
All data travels through the switch, which sends it on to the device it is meant for.
stations.challenge: Why is it called a star network? Sketch one with five computers on your worksheet.

stations.name: Advantages of star

tasks.q: One cable in a star network is cut. What happens?
a: Only the device on that cable loses its connection
The whole network stops working
Every device slows down
The data is automatically rerouted along another cable
tasks.fb: Each device has its own cable, so a cut cable only affects that one device. There is no other route, so the data can't be rerouted.

tasks.q: Why does a star network perform well?
a: The switch sends data only to the device it is meant for, so there is less unnecessary traffic
Every device receives every message
Data travels around a ring
It doesn't use any cables
tasks.fb: The switch forwards each piece of data only where it needs to go, which keeps traffic down.

bullets: If one cable fails, only that device is affected.
Easy to add a new device: just plug in one more cable.
Fast and reliable: the switch only sends data where it needs to go.
stations.challenge: One cable in a star network is cut. Which devices lose their connection?

stations.name: Disadvantages of star

tasks.q: What is the biggest weakness of a star network?
a: If the central switch fails, every device loses its connection
If one cable fails, every device loses its connection
It is hard to add new devices
Data can go the wrong way round the star
tasks.fb: The switch is a single point of failure: everything depends on it.

tasks.q: Why can a star network be expensive to install?
a: Every device needs its own cable back to the switch, which uses a lot of cable
Every device needs its own switch
Each computer needs a satellite dish
Star networks need a separate router for every room
tasks.fb: Running a separate cable from every device to the switch adds up to a lot of cable and installation work.

bullets: If the central switch fails, every device loses its connection. It is a single point of failure.
Every device needs its own cable back to the switch, so it uses a lot of cable, which costs money.
stations.challenge: What is the biggest weakness of a star network? Explain why.

stations.name: Joining star networks

tasks.q: An office has two star networks, each with its own switch. How are they joined together?
a: A cable links the two switches
Every computer is plugged into both switches
They are joined through the printer
Star networks can't be joined
tasks.fb: Linking the switches lets devices on one star reach devices on the other.

tasks.q: The link cable between the two switches is cut. What happens?
a: Devices can still talk to others on the same switch, but not to devices on the other switch
Every device loses its connection
Nothing changes
Only the two switches stop working
tasks.fb: Each star still works on its own. Only traffic between the two stars is cut off.

bullets: Bigger networks join several stars together by linking their switches with a cable.
Devices on different switches communicate over this link.
stations.challenge: The link cable between two switches is cut. Who can still talk to whom?

tasks.q: The cable between Sales 2 and Switch A is cut. Which devices can no longer reach the file server? Select all that apply.
tasks.fb: Only Sales 2 is cut off. Everyone else's cables and switches still work.

tasks.q: Switch A fails. Which devices can no longer reach the file server? Select all that apply.
tasks.fb: Everything plugged into Switch A loses its connection. Accounts and Conference are on Switch B with the server, so they are fine.

tasks.q: The link cable between the two switches is cut. Which devices can still reach the file server? Select all that apply.
tasks.fb: Accounts and Conference share Switch B with the server. Reception and Sales are stranded on Switch A.

tasks.q: Which single failure would stop every device from reaching the file server?
a: Switch B fails
Switch A fails
The cable to Reception is cut
The link cable between the switches is cut
tasks.fb: The server is plugged into Switch B, so if Switch B fails nobody can reach it. Cutting the server's own cable would do the same.

info.title: Hubs and switches
info.text: Older networks used hubs, which sent every piece of data to every device. Switches send data only to the device it is meant for, which is why star networks today perform well.

info.title: Adding a backup
info.text: Important networks often add a second switch or a second link cable, called redundancy, so the network keeps working if one part fails.

info.title: Hidden cables
info.text: In real offices, network cables run through ceilings, floors and walls to a comms cabinet, where they plug into switches. This is called structured cabling.

diagrams.title: Break a link and watch
diagrams.text: A message crossing a star and a mesh, then a cable cut in each. What still works, and what does not, is the whole comparison.

stations.name: Full mesh

tasks.q: What is a full mesh network?
a: Every device is connected directly to every other device
Every device connects to one central switch
Devices are connected in a single line
Devices connect only by Wi-Fi
tasks.fb: In a full mesh every device has a direct link to every other device.

tasks.q: How many cables are needed to connect four devices in a full mesh?
tasks.fb: Each of the 4 devices links to the 3 others: 4 × 3 = 12, but each cable joins two devices, so 12 ÷ 2 = 6.

bullets: Every device is connected directly to every other device.
Data can travel along many different routes to reach its destination.
stations.challenge: Count the cables in the picture. How many would you need to connect four devices in a full mesh?

stations.name: Mesh: pros and cons

tasks.q: One link in a mesh network fails. What happens?
a: The data is rerouted along another path
The whole network stops working
Every device loses its connection
Data waits until the link is repaired
tasks.fb: There are many routes between devices, so data simply takes a different one.

tasks.q: What is the main disadvantage of a full mesh network?
a: It needs a lot of cable and is hard to set up, so it is expensive
It has a single point of failure
Data can only travel one way
It can only connect two devices
tasks.fb: The number of cables grows quickly as devices are added, which makes a full mesh costly.

bullets: No single point of failure: if a link fails, data is rerouted along another path.
Can handle lots of traffic, because data is spread across many routes.
Needs a lot of cable and is difficult to set up, so it is expensive.
stations.challenge: Why would a bank's data centre choose a mesh rather than a star?

stations.name: Partial mesh: the internet

tasks.q: Why is the internet a partial mesh rather than a full mesh?
a: Connecting every router to every other router would need an impossible amount of cabling
Routers can only have one connection each
The internet doesn't use routers
A partial mesh has no single point of failure but a full mesh does
tasks.fb: Routers connect to several others, which gives plenty of alternative routes without linking every pair.

tasks.q: A router on the internet fails. What happens to data that was going to pass through it?
a: It is sent a different way through other routers
The whole internet goes down
It is deleted
It waits in the failed router until it is fixed
tasks.fb: Because the internet is a mesh, other routes are available around the failed router.

bullets: In a partial mesh, devices connect to several others, but not to all of them.
The internet is a partial mesh: routers link to a few other routers, so there is always another route.
stations.challenge: Why isn't the internet a full mesh?

stations.name: Wireless mesh

tasks.q: In a wireless mesh, what must be true of each wireless access point?
a: It must be within range of at least one other WAP
It must be plugged into the router with a cable
It must be in the same room as the router
It must connect to every device in the building
tasks.fb: WAPs pass data to each other by Wi-Fi, so each one needs at least one neighbour in range. Only one needs a cable.

tasks.q: What is a disadvantage of a wireless mesh compared with a wired network?
a: It can be slower and less reliable, because data hops between WAPs and walls cause interference
It needs much more cable
Devices must stay plugged in
It has no range limits
tasks.fb: Every hop between WAPs adds delay, and walls and other devices can weaken the signal.

bullets: Wireless access points connect to each other by Wi-Fi. Each one must be in range of at least one other.
Only one WAP needs a cable. Coverage is easy to extend, but data slows down as it hops between WAPs.
stations.challenge: Why might a wireless mesh be a good choice for a large house or an old building?

tasks.q: Sort each statement: does it describe a star or a mesh network?
items: The central switch is a single point of failure
Data can be rerouted if a link fails
Uses the least cable of the two
Each device connects to several others
A new device needs just one cable to the switch
tasks.fb: Use these to answer the worksheet question: why is a mesh network better than a star network, and when would you still choose a star?

tasks.q: Now choose. Which network would you fit in each of these places?
items: A classroom of 30 computers, on a tight budget
A hospital, where a failed link must not stop the data
A listed building, where no cable may be fixed to a wall
An office that plugs in a new computer most weeks
A park that needs Wi-Fi right across it
A bank's data centre, where staying up matters more than cost
tasks.fb: Each one turns on a single reason. Tight budget and one more cable point to a star. Surviving a broken link points to a full mesh. No cabling, or coverage to spread, points to a wireless mesh. In the exam the reason earns the mark, not the name.

info.title: Cables add up fast
info.text: Each new device in a full mesh needs a cable to every device already there, so the number of cables grows very quickly. That's why full mesh is rare for large networks.

info.title: Routes around damage
info.text: The internet grew from ARPANET, first connected in 1969. Its mesh-like design means data can find a way around broken links or failed routers.

info.title: Mesh Wi-Fi at home
info.text: Home mesh Wi-Fi systems use several units placed around a house. They pass data between each other so the signal reaches rooms that one router can't.
